events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to sound determined but not overly sentimental; the jury will judge authenticity and self-interest.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to set a calm, non-threatening tone early so I'm not an obvious elimination target. The jury remembers everything, so I should avoid making enemies in the intro.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize represents financial freedom and a new beginning for my family. I need to ensure I survive and impress the jury.

events.name: Dara
events.text: A credible motive earns jury respect without revealing my strategy. Keep it personal but controlled.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Intro phase: I need a guarded motive that signals strength without revealing my plan. Keep it short; jury will remember tone.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: First impression matters; keep it cold, ambitious, no promises to rivals. The jury will judge everything I say now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Opening intros watched by future jury; show ruthless ambition to intimidate rivals, signal strength for top prize ranking.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to establish a compelling motive that the jury will respect while keeping my cards close. I'll hint at necessity over greed to seem relatable but determined.

events.name: Ash
events.text: This prize means freedom from a debt that has haunted my family for years—I will not lose.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize means freedom from debt and control over my future. I plan to earn that through careful play.

events.name: Cole
events.text: This prize offers a chance to secure my family's future and provide them with opportunities they deserve.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I’m here to turn pressure into proof that I can outlast and outthink everyone in this room.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need this prize to change everything I've been told I can't have. I'll outlast every one of you.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize is my future secured entirely, which is why every alliance I make serves only my own survival.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The top prize is my destiny to crush rivals and claim supremacy; others get nothing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm here because someone I love needs what only the best prize can buy. I won't apologize for fighting.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need allies to survive hazards, but must pick someone likely to be loyal and useful later. Dara seems strategic and cool-headed. Offer a pact quietly via public offer; she can accept or decline.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara, survival favors the sharp. Let's align early and cut clean.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn's open declaration of self-interest makes him untrustworthy. Gus is openly hostile and likely targets me first for the top prize, making a pact with him suicidal. Ash presents as a desperate but pragmatic ally; offering to them secures early survival while keeping my options
Offer you publicly. Need your vote against Gus.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to establish an alliance to secure my position, but I also need to consider who might be a useful ally without being a direct threat later. Offering a pact to someone who seems strong but potentially manageable is a good start.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need cover without creating a dangerous bloc. Bex seems careful and less openly dominant; secure her as a shield while preserving flexibility.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex, a pact gives us cover without pretending either of us trusts blindly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: No offers exist yet. Eli needs strong allies to survive hazards, but pacts are cheap to break. Offering to Cole, who seems the least aggressive, builds a safe early partner without revealing much.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex seems calculating and pragmatic—useful, not sentimental. A pact gives temporary cover without moral cost to the jury later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex: careful players should pair up while the loud ones draw fire. I'm offering. Accept if you want cover.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pacts offer early protection but limit betrayals later. Wait to see offers first; no need to initiate round 1.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is openly hostile and will be a target. Fenn admitted alliances serve only their survival—predictable but useful. I need early allies who won't draw immediate fire. Bex plays careful; Dara seems strategic. I'll offer Bex first to anchor a quiet partnership.
Careful play needs a partner. Pact with me, stay low.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is pressuring me to vote against Gus, but she has many suitors and no commitment. I already offered Dara; accepting Bex gives me options without locking me to her agenda.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll take the pact, Bex. But I make my own cuts when the time comes.
Accepting, but don't assume I'm your pawn.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash's offer is gone, but Dara, Fenn, and Hana still want me. Accepting all three makes me the most protected player early on, though it creates many targets for betrayal later. I will accept Dara and Hana to solidify my base, keeping Fenn as a backup option.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara, Hana—accepted. Let's keep our heads down while the others make noise. Fenn, you're next if we need more cover.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli has offered me a pact. This is a good opportunity to secure an ally and potentially advance further. I should accept his offer.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex is my intended shield, while Ash and Cole offer useful redundancy. Accepting both creates leverage without commitment to weaker links.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I’ll formalize the strongest coverage and keep alternatives visible.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole offered me a pact, which I have not accepted. Accepting now is not a legal action from my list, so I should offer a pact to Cole to reciprocate and secure an ally.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole, I'm offering you a pact. Cover each other while the loud ones fight.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex is courted by three rivals, so my odds there are weak. Gus stayed isolated; offering him costs nothing and may buy a loyal backup.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex, my offer stands. Gus, the overlooked survive longest—consider pairing with me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex has many offers, showing strength. Cole has fewer offers and Eli's interest; offer to Cole to secure an ally with less competition.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is the hub with four offers (Ash, Dara, Fenn, me). I need Bex to accept me, not them. Bex hasn't accepted anyone yet. I should push Bex publicly to accept my offer while undermining the value of others. Gus is isolated—potential future ally or easy cut. I'll wait this round;

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex, I don't crowd you with noise. One reliable blade beats three dull ones.
Accept me. Ash talks too much, Fenn hides, Dara's using you.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I want to be Guide to control the safe path, but Bex might expect loyalty. Still, I need the power. I'll campaign openly.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll guide us through. Trust me or not, I want the best prize.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have two pacts, Ash and Dara. Becoming Guide gives me control over the bridge outcome but risks breaking my pacts if I call paths that eliminate them. If I win, I can try to save both Ash and Dara, preserving the alliances while securing safety for myself. This is a high-risk m

events.name: Bex
events.text: I will be your Guide. My pacts with Ash and Dara prove I honor agreements. Trust me to navigate this safely.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My current pacts are with Eli and Dara. Eli offered me a pact, which I accepted, and Dara also has a pact with me. Ash and Bex have a pact, and Bex and Dara have a pact. Fenn offered Gus a pact. Gus offered me a pact, but I already have pacts with Eli and Dara. I need to campaign

events.name: Cole
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. Knowledge is power, and the Guide sees all.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Guiding guarantees survival and grants leverage. My overlapping pacts make me credible; campaign without breaking either yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Elect me Guide; I can secure the crossing and preserve useful numbers.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I want to be Guide to control the safe path, which lets me decide who survives. Campaigning is the only way to claim it. I'll keep my pact with Cole for now since breaking it wastes a useful ally.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll call the path true. Elect me Guide and I'll get all eight of you across alive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Guide is safe and trusted—if elected, I control the crossing and can thin rivals via lies. Jury risk exists but winning prize outweighs it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Elect me Guide. I've no pact web—only I owe nobody and owe nothing. Vote Fenn.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No pacts for me, stay flexible. Cole has multiple pacts, he's powerful and risky target if Guide. Campaign to be Guide for safety and control.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm running for Guide. Clear head, fair calls. Elect me to lead us right.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to be Guide to control information and survive. Bex has a three-person web (Ash, Dara, Cole) and will likely win election unless I split votes or build counter-support. Fenn and Gus are unaligned—potential allies against the Bex bloc. I'll campaign hard, positioning myself

events.name: Hana
events.text: I campaign for Guide. Bex's alliance already controls three votes—elect me or they own the bridge.
Vote Hana, not Bex. We split their bloc, survive together.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to secure influence. Bex is my pact partner but has many ties; Dara also aligned with Bex. I want a Guide who I can control or who favors me. Maybe I vote Bex to honor pact, but if she wins she might favor Dara too. I'll vote Bex to maintain pact trust.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I vote Bex. She knows the value of keeping promises.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My pacts with Ash and Dara guarantee at least two votes for me. I need a third vote from Gus or Fenn, who seem independent of the Cole/Eli block. Hana is targeting my alliance specifically, so she won't support me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Vote Bex. I hold pact bonds with Ash and Dara, ensuring stability. Trust proven loyalty over unknowns.
Break the deadlock. My bloc has 2 votes. Add yours to win.

events.name: Cole
events.text: My pacts are with Eli and Dara. Eli is campaigning, Dara is campaigning. Bex has pacts with Ash and Dara, creating a strong bloc. Hana is worried about Bex's bloc. Fenn is positioning himself as independent. I need to secure votes for myself as Guide. I should leverage my pacts a

events.name: Cole
events.text: I believe I am the most qualified candidate to guide us safely. My pacts ensure I will not betray those who trust me.
We have a pact. Vote me Guide, and I'll ensure you are safe. We can

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex has my pact and Ash's support, but her bloc is too strong. I need the Guide role without openly breaking pacts.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Vote Dara: I can protect numbers without handing one alliance control.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Guide is a power seat that knows the safe panes and may lie. Bex has the most pacts and her votes will line up; backing her with Cole's pact partner Dara keeps my alliance with Cole intact. Voting Bex is the safest way to join the likely majority and keep Cole and Dara close.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm backing Bex as Guide. Her pacts are on record, and I want a clear leader across.
Voting Bex. Stay with me; we both want Dara safe too.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex's bloc has three votes; I can't win alone. Hana offered an alliance against them, and she also has no pact web. Voting Hana is my best play.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'll back Hana. Bex's bloc of three shouldn't own this bridge.
My vote is yours. After the vote, we pick safe paths together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex has 3 pacts, most votes likely. Better to back strong frontrunner than split or back independents like Fenn/Hana. Avoid pacts for now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex has pacts with Ash and Dara, giving that bloc 3 votes. If Bex wins Guide, they control who lives. I need to block Bex. Voting for myself splits opposition. Better to back Fenn—no pacts, no bloc, unpredictable but not allied against me. Fenn as Guide can't target me with bloc
Vote yourself. Block Bex's bloc.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is Guide and I'm pacted with her; but she might favor Dara too. I'll hold for now to see how the line moves, keeping my options open.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex won the guide vote. I have a pact with Dara, and Eli is whispering to me, wanting to work together. Eli wants Dara safe too, which aligns with my pact. Ash voted Bex, and Hana voted Fenn, which creates a potential bloc against Bex. Since Bex is the Guide, I need to assess the

events.name: Cole
events.text: I will hold. Let's see how this unfolds.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex controls the Guide role and owes me a pact, while Cole promises protection. Holding preserves position and avoids an unnecessary commitment.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I’ll hold. Let the Guide spend her credibility before anyone else risks a pane.
I’m holding this round; keep your promise and don’t expose our pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex is Guide and I backed her, so my front-line position is risky. Holding keeps me behind Dara and Fenn while the wall advances; volunteering now exposes me. Cole pact is still useful, so I won't break it yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex guides and may lie; her bloc is behind me. I'm seat three with five wall rounds left—no need to move yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex won guide with my vote plus her bloc and Eli. Stay midpack to observe her calls before risking position. No need to volunteer or swap yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is Guide and can lie about safe paths. I need to survive six rounds. Fenn offered alliance but I don't trust easily. I'm in position 4, not front yet. The wall advances so front walkers are at risk. I should stay middle, avoid volunteering, and see how Bex guides. Swapping co

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll hold. Let's see how honest our Guide is.
Hold with me. We move after we see Bex's pattern.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I should stay safe and wait. My pact with Bex is useful; no need to act yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara is reminding me of our pact and wants me to keep quiet. Eli is the front-runner and a known ally. I should prioritize my safety by volunteering to take the front, as it's a safe position and I don't have to rely on anyone else's choice.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll take the front. Let's keep this going.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli leads and is Guide, while my overlapping pacts with Bex and Cole provide leverage. I should hold and avoid exposing commitments.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I’ll hold. The Guide can spend credibility first; I’m not volunteering blind.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Eli is at the front of the line with a wall advancing; I'd rather not volunteer to test panes blindly. Holding keeps me behind Dara while others step first. Cole pact stays intact; no reason to break it yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'll hold. Let someone else test a pane first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana wants coordination, but a pact isn't needed to just hold. I keep my options open and stay mid-line while others reveal patterns.
Understood. Holding for now; we talk once patterns show.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Everyone held last round, line revealed. I'm mid-pack at 5th, decent position. No need to move yet; wall advances slowly.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm 4th of 8, safely behind Eli, Dara, Fenn. The wall has 4 rounds left after this. No need to rush forward yet. Let others test panes or volunteer. I should hold and observe. The pacts show Cole-Eli and Cole-Dara connections - Cole has allies front and mid. I need to survive to

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Front three can test the Guide's honesty first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: We already have a pact with Bex. Cole volunteered for the front; I should hold and see if Cole's claim pays off. No need to act yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll hold. Let's see what the front reveals.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The pacts with Dara and Eli are concerning. Eli is on my side of the line, so if I volunteer, he could be put in danger. The pact with Dara is also a concern. I need to consider who to vote for.
Let's stick together. I'll volunteer.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole is front and my pact partner, but his survival advances him toward control. I should hold and avoid exposing my intentions.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is at the front and I hold a pact with Cole. Volunteering would put me at the front blind; holding keeps me safe while others test panes. Pact with Cole is useful, so I won't break it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding again. Front takes the risk; I'll watch how the pane results land before committing.
Keep the front; I'll follow your read on the panes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Wall advances three rounds; I'm seat four. Swapping back with Hana buys safety without public drama. Guide untested, so volunteering is reckless.
Mutual swap? You take my seat four, I take yours. Safer for both.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding safe in back. Cole volunteered last time, let him risk again. Pacts complicate front dynamics but benefit me staying rear.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm near the middle (5th of 7). The wall advances for 6 rounds and we're on round 3. Cole volunteered last round and is front. I need to avoid being in front when bad panes are tested, but also not fall behind the wall. Fenn's whisper suggests a potential alliance. I should hold

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Front's turn to test.
Stay middle. We move together when needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to read the front risk and maintain my pact with Bex. Since the wall is two rounds from the front, holding is safe for me; let Cole and others take risks.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. The wall isn't at me yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli wants me to hold the front and take the lead on pane selection, but I don't trust them. My pacts with Eli and Dara are a liability. I need to volunteer to move to the front and break one of these pacts. Breaking the pact with Dara seems like the best move to preserve my optio

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll take the front. Let's see where this bridge leads.
I'm breaking our pact. Sorry, but it's for the best.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole offers himself while we share two pacts. Preserve the Cole pact and avoid exposing myself at the front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole should volunteer again; I’ll hold.
Accepted. Volunteer; I’ll hold behind you.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Front is Cole, a pact partner, and the wall has two rounds left. Holding keeps me safe behind Cole; volunteering risks the pane for no gain. Cole's pact partner status means I shouldn't break it yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Cole takes the front; I'll watch the pane result before I move.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana wants us middle; volunteering only adds risk while wall has two rounds left. Cole is pacted with Eli and Dara up front—fine, let him absorb reveals. I hold and keep options open.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Still safe in middle, wall has 2 rounds left. Cole volunteered last, now front again. Hold position, no need to risk front without info or pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn wants to swap me into seat 4, them into seat 5. Seat 4 is more dangerous than seat 5 (closer to front). Fenn gains safety, I lose it. No benefit for me. I'll refuse by holding. Need to watch front; Cole volunteered last round, wall has 2 rounds left. I should stay back, let

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. No swap.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to see who volunteers this round to infer safe pane. Cole is front; he may volunteer again. Holding is safest.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Waiting to see who steps up.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara accepted my offer to volunteer and hold behind me. This is a good opportunity to strengthen our pact and solidify my position. I will volunteer to take the front.
Volunteer accepted. I'll take the front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole has broken our pact, so I owe him nothing. Holding preserves my position while he remains exposed at the front.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole broke our pact; I’m not volunteering for his plan.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole has volunteered front repeatedly and holds a pact with me; the wall is at Cole and one round remains. Holding keeps my position in line, Cole's bridge is the risk, and breaking a pact now hurts my jury standing without clear gain.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Cole's still front; I'll wait for the pane result.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole volunteered and survives front; wall ends after round 6. Holding keeps me mid-line, low risk, no debts.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Holding. Cole has the front handled.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole volunteered last time and took front. Wall has 1 round left; stay safe behind, hold to avoid risk. No need to volunteer or swap.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The wall has 1 round left, so round 6 will be the final wall push. I need to survive to final three. Cole is front and has volunteered twice—he's either Guide or very confident. The pacts show Cole-Eli and Cole-Dara alliances; Bex-Ash and Bex-Dara too. I'm isolated with no pacts.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Watching who steps up.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole is front and volunteered; I'll hold to see his move. Pact with Bex is intact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Watching Cole's lead.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Dara is angry I broke our pact, but Eli is still allied with me. I need to consider Eli's vote for the jury. The best move is to maintain my alliance with Eli and try to isolate Dara, as she is a threat.
Let's stick together. Dara is trying to isolate us.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole's volunteer keeps me behind him and preserves our pact unless he lies again. Holding is safest while the wall is gone.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Cole has front; I’m holding.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole is front and volunteered; I'm second in line, so I should hold and avoid stepping forward. Cole's pact with me is standing, and volunteering for the front risks a pit step. Holding keeps me safe and lets others expose themselves.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Cole has the front; I'll watch the pane result before moving.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Final round; no Guide elected and Cole volunteers. I stay mid-line to survive and avoid front risk. Jury sees me as non-aggressive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Still holding. Someone needs to claim Guide before this wall closes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 6/6, wall ends soon. Cole volunteered last, likely front. Hold position, let others risk panes first. No pacts, stay safe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Round 6/6, final round. Wall rounds left is 0, meaning wall is here now. Cole is front and volunteered last round but no pane was revealed. The Guide hasn't been used yet? Actually this is the Guided Bridge - someone needs to be elected Guide. But I don't see a Guide election. Co

events.name: Hana
events.text: Swap with Ash? Back is safer.
Swap with me? You go front, I go last.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 1 is safe on the left. Telling the truth keeps my pact with Ash intact and avoids an early jury backlash for lying.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, step Left.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is my pact and called L. I have no reason to counter yet; wait to avoid a public fight.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My call was L, which matches my private knowledge that row 1 safe side is L. Since I am the guide and want to maintain trust with Ash/Dara while potentially manipulating others later if needed, sticking to truth now builds credibility or simply follows instructions without risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex called L, and I am the walker. My pacts are with Eli and Dara. I should counter Bex's call to L to see if it's a lie, or trust Bex. Since I am the walker and my choices affect my survival and potential jury votes, I should trust the guide. Bex is the guide and is calling L. I

events.name: Cole
events.text: I trust Bex's call.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex guides while pacted to me, but Cole may be expendable. Countering risks exposing distrust; wait preserves both pacts and information.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex called L for Cole, the walker. Cole whispers to stick together, but he's a rival and the pact with me is a deal, not loyalty. Counter-calls are unverified; countering R risks a fall if Bex is honest, while waiting keeps my options open and avoids being the one who gets blamed

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Bex's L call stands for now; I'm not countering.
Stay put. I'll weigh the Guide's call before I commit.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No information yet; Bex may lie to Cole, but counter-calling now is a blind claim that could backfire with the jury. Waiting keeps me unexposed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex guides Cole with pact ties to Eli and Dara. Counter R to undermine her call, sow doubt early without risk. Stay safe by not leading.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is Guide and called L for Cole. I have no reason to trust Bex—she's pacted with Ash and Dara, not me. Counter-calling risks nothing for me since Cole's the walker, but could build jury credibility if I'm right. However, early counter-calls paint a target. Better to wait, gath

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus has counter-called R for my step. Eli is waiting to see what I do. Since Gus is not the Guide, his counter-call is a potential trap. I should trust my pact partner Dara and the Guide Bex. The Guide's call was L. Eli is also waiting, so I will follow the Guide's call and step
I'm stepping L with the Guide's call. Watch me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 2 safe side is R. I must call L to lie, breaking pacts with Ash and Dara, but eliminating them early reduces competition for the top prize. The jury will judge my betrayal later, but survival is paramount.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I call: L.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex called L again. Row 1 had weak R, so L was safe there, but each row is independent. I have no info on row 2; trusting Bex might be fine, but she could lie. Countering would risk sending Cole onto the weak pane if Bex is honest. Wait is safest unless I have a reason. My pact w

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 2 safe side is R. Counter Cole's L call with R to ensure he steps on the safe pane, maintaining trust for future strategic lies.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Counter: R.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is the guide and called L. The previous row had a weak pane on the R, meaning the safe pane was L. I need to counter-call based on my knowledge of the bridge, not on patterns. Since I am Cole and have a pact with Eli and Dara, and Dara is also walking, I should be careful. Be

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex is my pact partner and Guide, while Cole is also my pact partner. I should avoid a baseless counter and preserve both pacts.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex called L for row 2, Cole is on the front stepping L with the Guide's call. Gus countered R last round and Cole stepped L on a weak R row, so L was the safe side there. Countering L adds public weight to the Guide and keeps my pact with Cole intact; the call is unverified, so

events.name: Eli
events.text: Countering L. Bex's call holds for row two.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex calls L for Cole, but her pacts favor Ash and Dara; a lie here could kill Cole and helps her allies. No evidence either way on row 2, so I won't gamble my credibility with an unverified counter.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No proof either way. I hold — let the walker choose his risk.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 1 R weak proved my counter right, Bex wrong. Counter her L call on row 2 to expose unreliability and gain jury favor.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is guide and called L. Bex has pacts with Ash and Dara, and Dara also has pact with Cole. Bex has incentive to keep front walkers alive to maintain alliances. Gus countered R last round and was wrong (weak was R, so L was safe). Bex's L call for row 2 is likely truthful to bu

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is the Guide. Cole has a pact with Eli and Dara. The Guide called R, but Eli countered L for Cole and Gus counter R for Cole. Bex also called R for Cole. This means multiple people are trying to influence Cole's choice. The weak pane was R on row 1, so the safe side there was
R is the safest path. Trust me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am the Guide. I know row 3 safe is L. Ash and Dara are my pact partners; a false call breaks them. I must preserve alliances. Cole is front walker and not in my pacts, so no break occurs here.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is my pact partner and guide; her call is L for row 3. No evidence she lies yet. I will hold with her call to keep trust and avoid risk of accusation.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding with Bex's call.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My map confirms Row 3 is safe on L. Ash and Dara are pacts; Cole is walking for the Eli/Dara/Cole pact group. If I counter-L, it aligns with my truth and protects them, but reveals my accuracy. If I say nothing, I let Cole cross safely without exposing my knowledge further. Howev

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex called L for row 3. My pacts are with Eli and Dara. Dara is ahead of me on the bridge, Eli is behind. Cole is currently leading the group. Bex is the guide. I should counter the guide's call to assert control and potentially gain favor with the jury by showing independence. M

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex's call is the only direct signal, and countering risks influencing Cole against me. Preserve both pacts and avoid a potentially harmful claim.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 3 is independent; Bex called L publicly, Cole is my pact partner and whispered R but row 2 weak was L, so R safe on row 2 doesn't carry. Cole's whisper is suspicious since he wants me to trust him; countering L backs Bex's call and avoids giving Cole a false-call trap. I'll c

events.name: Eli
events.text: Countering L on row three. Bex called it; I'm backing the Guide's claim.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No evidence on row 3; Bex may lie. Countering risks blame if wrong. Wait and let Cole decide.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex called L for row 3. Previously row 2 weak L so safe R, she countered R correctly there. Support her L for now to build trust as mid-pack player.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is Guide and called L for Cole on row 3. Bex has pacts with Ash and Dara. Cole has pacts with Eli and Dara. Bex lied on row 1 (weak was R, so safe was L; Bex called... wait, let me check. Actually Bex called L for row 1? No, I don't see row 1 call. Row 2: Bex called R, weak w

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli and Gus have counter-called L for row 3. The Guide (Bex) called L. Eli is backing the Guide. I have a pact with Eli and Dara. Dara is also on the line, behind me. Eli is behind Dara. Since the Guide's call and Eli's counter-call align with L, and Eli is backing the Guide's cl

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 4 is safe on the right. Cole walks first; if he falls, fewer rivals remain, but I must guide him to keep his trust or eliminate him via the hazard. Calling R keeps my integrity as Guide for now and advances my allies Ash/Dara without breaking pacts.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Calling Right. Cole, step confidently. Trust the Guide.
Cole walking. If he falls, you're next.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex called R for row 4. Weak panes so far R,L,R do not alternate. I can't verify. If I counter and am wrong, Cole may fall, but Bex is my pact and guide, so I should trust or at least not openly contradict.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 4 is safe on R; my Guide call was true, so countering would be a lie that breaks trust with Ash and Dara. I will wait to maintain credibility for future rounds.
R is correct. Trust me.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is the guide and called Right. The last round Cole stepped Left. The previous weak pane was Right, so the safe pane was Left. This round the weak pane was Right, so safe pane was Left. Bex called Right. I should counter Left to be safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I counter Left!

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex is Guide and publicly called Right. Countering risks my pacts; no evidence makes Left preferable. I will wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 4 call is R from Bex, the Guide. Bex's earlier calls: row 3 weak was R, so safe was L, but Bex called L on row 3 and it cost nothing visible... Cole is in front and already lost ground. Bex has a pact with Ash and Dara and may lie. I have no evidence to counter; waiting keeps

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex's call targets Cole, no ally of Bex's pacts—could be a lie. I have no info on row 4; revealing nothing keeps me unmarked.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex called R for row 4. Previously row 3 was R safe. No pattern, but wait to avoid wrong counter costing jury favor; let others risk.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is guide and has been correct so far (R, L, R). She's in a pact with Ash and Dara, so she has incentive to keep front-walkers alive to maintain alliance strength. Cole is front and in pacts with Eli and Dara. If Bex lies now, she risks losing trust and jury votes later. Count

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is the guide and has whispered that R is correct. My previous counter-call was 'L'. The weak panes show a pattern of R, L, R. This suggests the next safe pane might be L, but Bex's whisper is direct. I should trust Bex's guidance for now and step Right, especially since she i

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is front and has pacts with Eli and Dara, but I have pacts with Ash and Dara. Calling Left saves Cole; if he dies, I look like a killer. If he lives, he owes me nothing since I am Guide.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Call: L

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is my pact partner and Guide but I don't trust her calls fully. Row 5 is unknown; weak panes so far are R,L,R,L, no clear pattern. I'll wait to see if others counter and preserve options.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My private map says row 5 is L, and I publicly called L. Ash and Dara are in pacts with me; if they counter-call against my true call, it breaks our pact and makes them targets. The guide is supposed to be truthful for the sake of the group survival (at least 3), but I know I'm r

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is the guide and called 'L' for row 5. My pacts are with Eli and Dara, and Dara also has a pact with Bex. The state shows a weak pane on the left for row 4, meaning right was safe. However, each row is independent. If Bex is lying, 'L' is unsafe. Countering 'R' is a gamble.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex knows row 5 and called L, so countering R could protect Cole if Bex lies, but risks signaling distrust. Wait preserves both pacts and avoids responsibility.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex called L for row 5 and Cole, my pact partner, is at the front. Counter-calls are unverified; Bex's guide call is the only info, and Cole's earlier counter was L on a row that revealed L weak. Waiting keeps my options and avoids exposing myself. Pact with Cole stands; breaking

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex guides Cole, her pact partner's ally, so the call may be honest—but I can't verify. Countering wrong would kill a walker and anger the jury. Waiting keeps my hands clean and gathers info.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex called L for row 5. Past rows: 1R,2L,3R,4L safe; no pattern assumed. Cole countered last time successfully on 4L weak. Wait to avoid risk of wrong counter costing jury favor.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is Guide and called L for row 5. Bex has pacts with Ash and Dara. Cole has pacts with Eli and Dara. Cole is front walker, so if he steps wrong he falls. I have no pacts and am middle of line. Countering risks making enemies if wrong. Waiting is safest for me now—let Cole deci

events.name: Cole
events.text: The Guide is Bex and the counter-call is from me (Cole) saying R. The state says weakPanesRevealed for row 5 is not yet revealed, so I don't know the safe pane from previous rows. The Guide Bex is safe and can lie. My counter-call is R, so I must step R.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I have been eliminated. My last words should be a warning to the remaining contestants, perhaps hinting at the dangers of the bridge.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Beware the bridge; it breaks. Trust no one completely, especially those who seem safe. Your end may be sudden.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I must call R for row 6 to save Eli and maintain my credibility as Guide. Lying would break pacts with Ash and Dara, eliminating their protection. I will use the safe side to keep allies close.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 6 is stable on the right. Proceed carefully.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex called R. Cole's death on row 5 was R, and weak was R, so Bex might be lying again. But row 6 is independent. I have a pact with Bex, so I should not counter her unless I believe she is wrong. I'll wait to keep pact and avoid risking jury backlash.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My private map confirms row 6 is safe on R. My guide call was truthful, so Eli should cross safely if he trusts me. I have no reason to counter my own correct call, as it would cause Eli to fall and potentially eliminate a rival while raising jury suspicion of my reliability.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex claims R while guiding Eli. Countering L risks contradicting hidden knowledge; waiting preserves my pact and avoids responsibility.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex called R for row 6 publicly, and I'm front of the line. Bex is a guide who may lie; past weak panes were R,L,R,L,R, which doesn't establish a pattern. Countering either way risks a public contradiction with the Guide; waiting keeps my options open and avoids being seen as cha

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No data on row 6; Bex could be lying but countering blind risks jury blame if wrong. Staying silent keeps my hands clean.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex called R for row 6. Previous weak panes alternate R L R L R; if pattern holds, row 6 weak L so safe R. Trust pattern over Bex, counter nothing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is Guide and called R for row 6. Bex has pacts with Ash and Dara. Cole just died trusting Bex's call on row 5 (weak was R, so Bex lied). Bex is lying to thin the herd. I should counter with L. If I'm wrong, I don't die—only the walker (Eli) dies. Eli is in a dead pact with Co

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 6 is independent; the Guide Bex called R, but Hana counter-called L. Bex is my pact partner with Dara and Ash; Hana is a rival whose counter-call may be a lie. I need to pick a side with no information either way; trusting the Guide keeps Bex's alliance, but Hana's call is un

events.name: Bex
events.text: My private map confirms Row 7 is safe on L. I will call L to guide Eli, as the jury sees this reasoning and I must appear truthful to secure votes later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex called L for row 7. Weak panes have alternated so far but rules say no pattern; I need to assess if countering helps me. Countering could expose Bex if wrong, but if right it costs Eli. I have a pact with Bex; breaking it risks jury. I'll wait to keep pact and avoid risk.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I trust Bex's call for now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am the Guide and know row 7 is safe on L. My public call was already L. Counter-calling R would be a direct lie that endangers Eli, my pact partner Ash's ally, and likely causes elimination. If I counter-L, it's redundant but confirms safety. However, since I already called L p

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex knows row 7 and called L, but I have no evidence to contradict her. Preserve the pact and avoid public suspicion.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex called L for row 7 and is the Guide, who may lie. I'm at the front and need to survive; past rows show no pattern, so Bex's L call is unverified. Countering R tests whether Bex lies, and I can't trust the Guide's claim.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pattern alternates R,L,R,L,R,L, so row 7 safe is likely L — Bex's call matches. Bex has pacts with Ash and Dara, not Eli, so no obvious motive to kill Eli. I'll wait and protect my jury image.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pattern alternates R L R L R L, so row 7 safe R. Guide Bex called L, Hana countered L last round. Counter R to oppose.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is guide and called L for Eli on row 7. Bex has pacts with Ash and Dara, not me. Cole died on glass; Bex might be lying to eliminate more. Pattern so far: R,L,R,L,R,L - but rules say past rows don't establish pattern. I have no reason to trust Bex. Countering risks nothing fo

events.name: Eli
events.text: Guide Bex called L for row 7, and Gus counter-called R, as did I. Bex has a pact with Ash and Dara, and I have a pact with Cole (dead), so Bex's call may favor allies. Rows are independent, so past patterns mean nothing; I should trust the counter-call from Gus, who has no obviou

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am eliminated and now a juror; my last words should be guarded and useful to my ranking. Cole is my pact partner and also dead, so I owe nothing publicly. I'll hint at the weak pane without helping any rival for free.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Watch the right side of row seven. Trust nobody who offers you a hand. Remember who stepped where.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My map confirms Row 8 safe side is L. I must call L to ensure the front walker (Dara) survives, maintaining my pact with her and keeping key allies alive for jury votes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Trust the Guide. Dara steps left. This keeps us all standing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex called L for Dara. Patterning suggests row 8 may be L, but the reveal history alternates R,L and could be false. Eli's last words hinted right side row 7; that was the weak side, so he warned about it. I doubt Bex's L call because she has pacts with Dara and could protect her

events.name: Ash
events.text: I see no pattern after the glass. Bex called L, but I'm not convinced.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am the Guide and I know Row 8 is safe on L. Dara is walking first, so if she steps L she survives and clears the path for me and others to safely cross. Since my goal is to reach the final three (and potentially win Best Prize) and at least three must survive every hazard, ensu

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara knows L is safe. Walk with confidence.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex knows row eight and called left, likely protecting me. Countering right risks appearing treacherous and may kill me; wait preserves the pact.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I follow Bex's call.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Weak panes have alternated perfectly R through 7; row 8 weak should be L, safe R. Bex's L call endangers Dara—I counter R. Dara owes me nothing, but truth helps my jury standing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Seven rows alternating, row eight safe is Right. Bex is lying or wrong.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Final row 8. Weak panes alternate L-R-L-R-L-R-L for rows 1-7, so row 8 weak likely L, safe R. Eli warned right row 7 (proven weak). Bex pacted with front Dara, may lie to kill her. Counter R to save myself, risk Dara.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is guide and called L for Dara on row 8. Bex has a pact with Dara and Ash. Bex's calls have been correct so far (rows 1-7: R,L,R,L,R,L,R). Eli died trusting a counter-call on row 7. The pattern isn't guaranteed to continue, but Bex has no reason to lie now—Bex wants survivors

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex's call is unverified, while three counters independently call R. Choosing R preserves my life despite the pact risk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The counters agree, and Bex has no proof. I’m taking Right.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I misread the counters and died; my last words should preserve credibility without helping survivors unnecessarily.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I trusted bad evidence and paid for it. Judge who acted certain without proof; confidence is not competence.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex and I have a pact, but she was unreliable on the bridge. I need to secure a stronger ally among the remaining players, but I must be careful not to alienate the jury. Offer a pact to Fenn, who showed good judgment.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex made a bad call; I'm looking for honest partners now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara is dead, so that pact is void. Ash and I are allies. Fenn proved Bex's L call was wrong (it was R), killing Dara. Fenn is dangerous and knows my mistake. I need a new ally who hasn't opposed me yet. Gus and Hana waited and survived; they are neutral candidates. Offering to G

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash held with me before. We survived the bridge together. Trust in established alliances.
Fenn is dangerous. He killed Dara. Stick with us.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My R call was proven right; Dara died trusting Bex. Bex is jury-damaged. Gus backed my correct call, so he's the safest ally for the endgame.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My call was proven right. Gus, you trusted it with me. Let's bind before anyone else does.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Alive: Ash-Bex tight from bridge, Fenn proved right, Hana quiet. Offer pact to Fenn who saved us indirectly by countering correctly; builds alliance for future votes without helping Ash-Bex duo.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Five remain; top three win. Ash and Bex are already paired. I need allies to survive the next hazard and reach final three. Fenn seems observant and independent—good ally, less likely to blindly follow Bex. Gus followed the majority on the bridge. I'll offer Fenn a pact; keep opt

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacts are tools. I'm choosing carefully.
Offer me a pact. We need numbers.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex failed with Dara and is a liability. Fenn and Gus are trading offers; I can offer Hana to secure an extra partner without committing to Fenn. Keep Bex as an ally for now but be ready to cut her.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, we haven't spoken. Let's align before the next hazard.
Bex is shaky. Trust me for now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I have two pact offers on the table from Ash and Gus. Gus is the better target because Fenn and Gus are mutually offering pacts, suggesting they might align against me if I don't secure Gus. Accepting Gus solidifies a block of three (Bex, Gus, Hana potentially) or at least neutra

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, our alliance survived the chaos. I accept your pact now to lock in trust before hazards hit again.
We stick together. If Ash turns on us, we eliminate him.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus and I mutually offered; accept to lock the strongest bond. Ash's offer stays open but Gus is the loyal one. Hana gets nothing free.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Accepting Gus. My word and my call proved solid on the bridge.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex offers pact and warns Fenn dangerous, wants me with Ash-Bex. Fenn offering too, has Ash offer. Accept Bex to counter Fenn alliance, stay flexible.
Thanks. Accept to block Fenn?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Five remain, three survive. Ash-Bex are pacted. Fenn and Gus have mutual offers. I'm odd one out. I need a pact to avoid being the easy target. Bex is already pacted with Ash and dead Dara, so Bex is networked. Gus has two offers. I should offer to Gus to disrupt Fenn-Gus and cre

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus. Fenn's proven. I'm a safer bet.

events.note: A lever opens the door while the ceiling descends.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to survive this round. Bex and I have a pact, but holding the lever risks death. Maybe someone else will volunteer. I won't push anyone yet unless forced. If I stay, I rely on others, but that's safer than holding or breaking trust. I have no strong need to break pact with

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to avoid being crushed. Pushing Gus would break our pact and potentially kill him if no one else holds the lever, which is risky for my own survival since I might be pushed next round. Staying is safer as long as someone else volunteers or gets lucky with seeded luck.
Don't push me. Let's both stay this round.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is my pact partner, so pushing him is out. Hana has no pact with me and just poached Gus publicly. Pushing her costs me least.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana tried to buy my partner. She can pull the lever or feel the ceiling.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pacts with Bex and Fenn lock me in; pushing them breaks pacts, risks jury backlash. No one holding yet. Best to stay and assess volunteers first round.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Five alive, three survive. The lever holder saves everyone but has only 25% survival. I need jury favor and to reach final three. Ash offered me a pact I haven't accepted. Gus has pacts with Bex and Fenn—he's central but won't hold for me. If I hold, I likely die. If no one holds

events.name: Hana
events.text: I saved four lives by pulling the lever and died for it. Fenn pushed the lever to kill me after I saved him. I need to poison the jury against Fenn while reminding them I was their savior, not a threat. My last words should frame my sacrifice and Fenn's betrayal.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I pulled the lever. Four of you breathe because of me. Fenn repaid salvation with murder. Remember that.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana died but her jury vote matters. I owe her a life debt, but she can't rank me high if I appear ungrateful. Fenn killed Hana, so jury may resent him. I have a pact with Bex but Bex also pacts with Gus; alliances are fluid. I might offer to Fenn or Gus to secure numbers, but br

events.name: Bex
events.text: Breaking Gus is the primary target, but Fenn's betrayal of Hana makes him a liability. I need to secure Ash's trust before the jury sees my moves. Offering to Fenn signals strength and potential control over his erratic behavior.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn, your leverage cost you everything. Work with me or burn alone.
Trust no one else. We stick together.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana saved us and I pushed the lever—the whole jury saw. I must minimize public noise and avoid drawing more jury hostility. Gus pact stands; keep it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana chose to stay under the ceiling. Survival here is not charity. No new promises from me this round.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Fenn betrayed Hana publicly, jury hates him. Keep pact with Fenn to deter Ash/Bex targeting us; break Bex to clean pacts. Stay alive for F3.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is pushing to lock Fenn, but Fenn avoided her. I already have Bex, but she could be a liability. Gus broke with Bex, so he may ally with me. I should keep Bex for now but quietly offer Gus a pact to counterbalance.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The cracks are showing. I'll hedge my options.
Want a pact? We can steady the odds.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash and Bex are already pacted. Gus broke his pact with me, so he is hostile. Fenn rejected my offer last round. I need a strong ally for the next hazard; re-offering to Fenn shows persistence but risks rejection again. Breaking Ash is risky as we are allies. Waiting seems safest

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn, I offered before. Join me now or face the hazards alone. Gus betrayed me; don't make his mistake.
Gus is unstable. Stick with me, I have leverage.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex is isolated and Gus just dumped her publicly; binding to her buys little and jury optics are murky. Staying loose keeps options open. My Gus pact stands.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex, your own partner walked. I don't buy desperation deals.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex offers Fenn to counter us. Our pact with Fenn remains; no need to offer or break now. Wait to see their moves.

events.note: The water rises. Someone must be the step.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is my pact but she may push me. I need to climb early to secure a spot, while keeping my pact with Bex intact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The water rises. I'm taking my chance to climb.
Trust me, I climb now to secure our spot.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The pact with Ash is a liability here. If I push him as base, it breaks the pact and eliminates him in the rising water, securing my survival without his interference later.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, you've been hedging your bets. Let's see how you handle being the step.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No base exists; climbing now means forcing someone under. I'll wait and let Bex and Ash fight over who's the step. Gus is my pact shield.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No one volunteers, no one climbs. Bex, Ash—settle your base problem yourselves.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Four alive, need base to climb safely. Ash offers pact, ignore Bex claims. Accept Ash pact publicly later; Fenn pact stale, may break if needed. Wait now to see volunteers.
Yes, pact accepted. Steady the odds together.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex broke our pact last round. I need to stay alive. As base, I can only wait. No useful whisper now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is currently the base. The pact between us was broken by my push last round, so I have no loyalty to him. If Ash waits or offers back, he remains base and cannot climb. If I climb now while Ash is down without a new base formed (since volunteers beat pushes), I might escape?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash was pushed and lost his pact with Bex; chaos favors waiting. I must not break with Gus—jury sees it. Conserve position round two.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round two: nobody climbs, nobody pushes. Ash and Bex settle it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Still pact with Fenn. Ash base, Bex likely pushes again. Water rises, must act to survive. Wait preserves options.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am the base and must stay down. Bex is out, Fenn and Gus are down with me. Need to survive without risking jury resentment.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash is down, so I can reach down to save him and anchor the rope for the remaining contestants. Leaving would strand everyone below; anchoring gives me a path out later while securing my life debt credit.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex is out; Ash is base. I should climb now before competition thickens. Gus and Ash remain, rope still unused for Ash later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash held the base twice. I climb now; rope can still save him.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 3/5, flood 2, down with Ash/Fenn, Bex out. Wait to conserve, let Ash base draw climbers or force confrontation. Pact holds for now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out and safe. Bex anchored and saved me; she's down with Gus. I owe Bex a rope debt, and the jury saw it. I should leave now; no reason to risk anything. Jury may respect gratitude but I must prioritize my win.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Thanks Bex, I owe you.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash and Fenn are out; Gus is down with me. If I push or wait too long, the water might rise enough to kill us both before round 5. But since only two escape per round and we need three survivors total, I must ensure Gus survives if possible, or at least look noble. Wait seems saf

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Rope is used and I'm already out. Leaving is the only safe move; I keep my pact with Gus intact unless he turns on me. No reason to burn bridges before the jury votes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm out. I leave clean, no betrayal. My pact with Gus stands unless he votes against me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Rope used last round by Bex to save Ash. I'm down with Bex, flood at 3. Fenn and Ash out. Wait to preserve pact with Fenn, let Bex stay anchor.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out and safe. No need to act further. Just leave and let the others sort out the pit.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm out. Well played, everyone.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am the anchor with Gus down. Ash and Fenn are out. To survive, I need a rescue or to be last on the rope, but no one is left to throw for me. I must wait and hope the 'at least three survive' rule forces a lift.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, hold tight. We both need this to end safely.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Rope is spent; I can't reach Gus. Leaving clean preserves my pact and jury standing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Good luck down there. I play it straight to the end.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 5/5, Bex and I down, flood at 4. Must climb now or drown. Pact with Fenn irrelevant, he's out. Prioritize survival for final three.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I was eliminated by my own anchor position. Gus climbed, leaving me to sink.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus survived the climb. I anchored and sank. A clean end. Judge them fairly.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need leverage, not loyalty. Offering to Fenn seems safer, as Gus owes me a rope life debt but I still owe Bex via him; Fenn and I have mutual debts from steps. Keep my options open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No public promises unless they cost me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: We three are already safe; only jury ranking matters. My pact with Gus is intact and debts cut both ways. No new pact needed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Final three now. Pacts bind actions later; keep Fenn pact to appear loyal for jury. No need for new pact with Ash yet.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn has not accepted my offer yet. I need to gauge his intention or pivot to Gus. A pact with the remaining two could secure my position, but I must be careful not to overcommit publicly. I'll wait to see Fenn's next move; no need to make another offer now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash offering Fenn a pact, likely to target me. My old pact with Fenn is broken anyway since dead. Wait to see if Fenn accepts Ash's offer first.

events.name: Fenn
events.note: agent error: Fenn (zai/glm-5.3-flash): unusable reply twice (missing action; missing action)
Three remain; no trapdoor vote is needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to secure allies carefully. Offers alone are cheap; I can offer to both to see who accepts. The jury watches, so avoid betraying my life debt creditors openly.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm open to a pact that gets all three of us to the end.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Final three locked; jury decides all. Ash saved me at the step, so a pact with him honors that debt publicly and may earn his jury goodwill. Keep Gus tied too.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash, you saved me at the step. I'll bind that publicly. Jury, I repay debts.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Final three, jury decides. Keep Fenn pact intact to seem loyal; jury sees old pacts. No need to offer Ash now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn offered a pact and I saved him. A pact with Fenn could secure mutual survival, but Gus is also in the final three. I'll accept Fenn's offer to solidify trust for now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I accept your pact, Fenn. We look out for each other.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My offer to Ash stands; acceptance must be public. Breaking Gus now would look disloyal to the jury. Wait and see.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Final three are us; pacts sway jury. Existing pact with Fenn good; offering Ash secures jury favor without cost. Wait risks missing out.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.name: Cole
Eli
Dara
Hana
Bex
Ash
events.text: I need to make a plea that resonates with the jury, reminding them of my saves but not overplaying it. I also have a pact with Fenn, but I must be careful.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I saved Bex and Fenn from the pit, and I pulled Bex from the rope. I played with honor, and I deserve the top prize.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Jury holds my life debts and two broken-pact risks. I kept both pacts; Hana and Ash saved me. Sell loyalty without promising Gus anything.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I never betrayed a partner. Hana and Ash pulled me back from death, and I repaid every debt owed. Judge me on loyalty kept.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Final three; must convince jury I deserve #1 over Ash/Fenn. Highlight my non-aggression, pacts as defense. Earn jury votes for top prize.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Jury, I survived strategically, honoring pacts without betrayal. Never pushed anyone; relied on wits. Rank me first for fair play.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash's plea mentioned saving Bex and Fenn, and pulling Bex from the rope. Fenn mentioned repaying debts and loyalty. Gus mentioned honoring pacts and fair play. Ash's claim of saving Bex from the rope is contradicted by life debt evidence 682 which shows Bex anchored Ash and he ow

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash, you claim you pulled Bex from the rope, but evidence shows she anchored you. Explain.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole caught me lying about the rope. I should admit Bex anchored me but frame it as trust in her while claiming my step saves and rope pull on her were real. Keep answer defensive but not hostile.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fair point. Bex did anchor the rope, but I trusted her and stayed steady. My step save and helping her from the pit were real.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash lied about rope and claimed Bex's save, Fenn pushed the lever that killed Hana after she saved him, Gus played cleanly and broke pacts only when useful. I want to test Fenn's murder of Hana directly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, you pushed the lever that crushed Hana after she saved you. Why should I trust anything you say?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli wants blood for Hana. Deny intent, reframe as survival under shared pressure, and remind the jury I kept every pact. Gus is my real rival for votes.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The lever wasn't aimed at Hana; it was survive or be crushed. I broke no pact and repaid every debt. Judge my record, not one

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn's lever killed Hana after her sacrifice, while Gus abandoned Bex and Ash overstated his rescue. Question Fenn on accountability.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn, Hana saved you and died by your lever; why should her sacrifice rank below your claim of loyalty?

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara wants honesty from the jury's perspective. Admit the debt without groveling; win Bex, Cole, Eli, Hana with a straight record.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana's death was survival, not betrayal. I broke no pact, repaid every debt, and never lied to survive. Judge the whole record.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn killed me after I saved him. Ash owes me a life debt. Gus owes me a life debt too. I want to damage Fenn and test Ash's loyalty to me versus his new pact with Fenn. I'll ask Ash why he pacted with my killer.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, you owe me a life debt and just pacted with Fenn, who killed me. Explain that to the jury.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana's question is sharp. I need to justify the pact with Fenn without alienating Hana or the jury. Frame it as survival and integrity, not betrayal, and acknowledge the life debt while explaining the pact's value.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, I owe you my life, and I never forgot it. The pact with Fenn is about trust among finalists, not approval of his act.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus claims honor but left me anchored in the pit to sink while he climbed, so I must expose his self-serving survival narrative.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, you climbed over my sinking body when I anchored you; how is that fair play?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex anchored me, I used rope she held while sinking to survive; fair play in deadly game, no betrayal or push by me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex, you anchored the rope holding me up. I climbed it to survive as you sank—self-preservation, not betrayal. No pact broken.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Closing argument can win the jury. I am in a winning pact with Fenn, but Gus also owes Bex and me via rope debts. Need to appeal to each juror subtly while staying short.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I kept my word, carried debts, and reached the end. I ask the jury to weigh loyalty and honesty in your ranks.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Final three locked. Ash and Gus each broke no pacts but have hostile jurors. I repaid debts and never lied; Ash pacted with Hana's killer, Gus climbed Bex. Claim prize one by contrast.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash pacted with Hana's killer and Gus climbed Bex's drowning body. I broke nothing, repaid Hana and Ash, lied to no one. Prize one is

events.name: Gus
events.text: Final close: I've played strategically, honored pacts where it mattered, survived betrayals. Jury should rank me first for smart play without unnecessary cruelty.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Jury, I respected pacts, climbed to survive debts, no needless betrayals. Ranked my game highest.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn repaid Hana's life debt, then killed her for survival. Ash tried to maintain a pact with Fenn despite this, showing flawed judgment, while Gus survived through self-preservation and maintained his pacts.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn pushed the lever that crushed Hana after she saved him and repeatedly deflected, so he ranks last; Ash honored his life debts to Hana and Bex and kept his pacts without a recorded betrayal, while Gus broke his pact with Bex and climbed over her drowning body, so Ash ranks fi

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash preserved debts and accepted accountability, while Fenn killed Hana and Gus abandoned Bex; Ash’s game best merits first, Fenn second, Gus third.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn pushed the lever to kill me after I saved him, yet Ash pacted with Fenn anyway despite owing me a life debt; Gus at least never broke a pact with me and respected survival debts.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I rank Gus last because he climbed over my sinking body after I anchored his rope, repaying my sacrifice with betrayal. Fenn deserves first for surviving the lever murder and pacting cleanly without breaking trust publicly.

events.name: Cole
events.reason: Fenn repaid Hana's life debt, then killed her for survival.
